system.summary: One number per letter, separated by dots. Vowels 1-5 (a e i o u) and again 10 20 30 40 50; consonants in alphabetical order from 11 (b c d f g l m n p q r s t z = 11-24), so 20 is both e and q. A double stroke after a group doubles the consonant. Numbers from 80 up are codes for common words and names.

diacritics.note: a double stroke after a group doubles the consonant

system.doubled_letters: marked by a double stroke after the group
system.notes: Not the Riva table of targets/riva1722. The alphabetical order of the consonants is derived from the values, not seen in a key sheet. nomenclator.entries counts the distinct numbers of 80 and over; ten have a value from the glosses, none is counted read.

prior_solution.where: A contemporary hand deciphered about 55% of the cipher on the letters themselves (234 of 426 units: the foot of c. 17r, and between the lines on cc. 1 and 13v). For the rest, priority is NOT established: Lindgren, Il Saggiatore musicale 23/2 (2016), 277-374, uses this file and treats Riva's recruiting of singers; it was not seen (not open access) and may quote the Borosini passage. Lindgren and Timms 2003 (searched): not these letters.

solution.what: Ciphertext-only annealing on the 31 May 1721 letter (104 groups): no reading. The foot gloss was not noticed.
The Riva table (K3) tried on the 31 May letter as a control: 597 of 5,000 shuffled keys as good. Not that table.

Key K21 (22 letters and one code) taken from the contemporary gloss at the foot of c. 17r, which covers the first half of the 31 May letter. Applied to the second half, which has no gloss: 31 of 36 units; whole letter 93 of 104.

Sweep of the Starhemberg file and of Riva's other correspondents: two more letters in this cipher found (14 Jun 1721, 21 Dec 1720), neither tagged as cipher in the catalogue, both partly glossed between the lines.
K21 unchanged, one decode each: 14 Jun 1721, 249 of 289 units, 97 of 110 without a gloss, 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys; 21 Dec 1720, 31 of 33 as first counted.

Check by Daniel Bourdeau on issue 432: the 31 May figures hold (104 units, 93 read, held-out 31 of 36); the two letters of the comment could not be checked without files; 20 = e needs a full-scale recheck, since the 1719 table has 20 = qu; this cipher to have its own entry.

For this folder: the consonants are in alphabetical order from 11, which makes 20 = q by position as well as e among the tens, and gives 11 = b and 24 = z. One unit of the 1720 letter downgraded (ziffere): 30 of 33. One crop of the 31 May letter looked at for the form of 20: no clear separate sign. Full-scale recheck not done.
Lindgren 2016 not open and not seen; Lindgren and Timms 2003 searched through a fetch tool: these letters are not printed there.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Every key value comes from the contemporary decipherment written at the foot of the 31 May 1721 letter. The unglossed parts of the three letters were then read with that key unchanged.

texts.label: Starhemberg to Riva, 21 December 1720
texts.summary: A two-line postscript in cipher: 'Lei continui di scrivermi in ziffere spesso', keep writing to me in cipher, often. The earliest dated use of this cipher in the file; the writer asks Riva to use it.

texts.label: Starhemberg to Riva, 31 May 1721
texts.summary: His return to England is certain, as Ambassador. In cipher: the Duke of Modena does well to continue his devotion to the House of Austria, the more so as examples show that those who have been faithful to it have gained very great advantages; he will say more on this point when he arrives. The second half is not covered by the contemporary gloss.

texts.label: Starhemberg to Riva, 14 June 1721
texts.summary: He asks about the South Sea affair and whether an opera company will be formed in London this year. In cipher: Borosini, in Vienna, sings tenor and has no equal in Europe; he would join the company if asked for in the name of the King or of the company, and a letter of request to Starhemberg would do. A certain Colman has arrived to serve under St Saphorin, the British minister: is he the son of 'Hoffman'? He wants all the talk of court and nation in London on Vienna's conduct towards 'Sig. Cnigt' (Robert Knight of the South Sea Company, by sense). Context: the Royal Academy of Music's recruiting of singers; Francesco Borosini did sing in London in 1724-25.
